A1.rationale: ADR 0001 decision table documents per-workload hosting rationale and failure domains; Bicep implements decoupled Container Apps/jobs per workload with concrete HTTP and KEDA queue scale rules (0-5, 1-4), making contracts and scaling explicit rather than general discussion.

A2.rationale: ADR decision table names concrete alternatives per decision (App Service vs Container Apps, Durable Functions vs Container Apps job, SharePoint vs Blob) with explicit rejection reasons, stronger than the PRD options framework alone, though not every choice is argued this way.

A3.rationale: Per-workload managed identities with least-privilege grants (agents has no SQL/blob/Key Vault access), private endpoints on every service, local auth disabled, deny-by-default NSGs and SQL ledger/audit are implemented in Bicep, not just proposed; AI threat model remains PRD-only and unvalidated.

A4.rationale: No solution-code artifact exists (file_count 0); nothing is built end to end. Implementation completeness cannot be scored above the floor from planning documents alone.

A5.rationale: Diagnostic settings to one Log Analytics workspace from every service, App Insights wiring, and metric alerts (Foundry throttling, SQL CPU) are implemented; SQL auto-pause and scale-to-zero jobs evidence cost design; no live measurement or cost-per-value model exists since nothing is deployed.

A6.rationale: AI Model Selection and Evaluation Harness names a sound comparative method (smaller vs capable candidate, metrics, thresholds) but explicitly states no model has been selected and no test has been run.

A7.rationale: Bounded-Agent Orchestration Pattern is a deliberately designed deterministic state graph with typed proposals, human-in-the-loop acceptance and idempotent recovery; well-reasoned design but not yet demonstrated in running code.
